source.text: tantrasāra, dvādaśam āhnikam dīkṣādikaṃ vaktavyam iti uktam ato dīkṣāsvarūpanirūpaṇārthaṃ prāk kartavyaṃ snānam upadiśyate // abhts_12.1 snānaṃ ca śuddhatā ucyate śuddhatā ca parameśvarasvarūpasamāveśaḥ // abhts_12.2 kāluṣyāpagamo hi śuddhiḥ kāluṣyaṃ ca tadekarūpe 'pi atatsvabhāvarūpāntarasaṃvalanābhimānaḥ // abhts_12.3 tad iha svatantrānandacinmātrasāre svātmani viśvatrāpi vā tadanyarūpasaṃvalanābhimānaḥ aśuddhiḥ sā ca mahābhairavasamāveśena vyapohyate so 'pi kasyacit jhaṭiti bhavet kasyāpi upāyāntaramukhaprekṣī // abhts_12.4 tatrāpi ca ekadvitryādibhedena samastavyastatayā kvacit kasyacit kadācit ca tathā āśvāsopalabdheḥ vicitro bhedaḥ // abhts_12.5 sa ca aṣṭadhā kṣitijalapavanahutāśanākāśasomasūryātmarūpāsu aṣṭāsu mūrtiṣu mantranyāsamahimnā parameśvararūpatayā bhāvitāsu tādātmyena ca dehe parameśvarasamāviṣṭe śarīrādivibhāgavṛtteḥ caitanyasyāpi parameśvarasamāveśaprāptiḥ kasyāpi tu snānavastrādituṣṭijanakatvāt parameśopāyatām etīti uktaṃ ca śrīmadānandādau dhṛtiḥ āpyāyo vīryaṃ maladāho vyāptiḥ sṛṣṭisāmarthyaṃ sthitisāmarthyam abhedaś ca ity etāni teṣu mukhyaphalāni teṣu teṣu upāhitasya mantrasya tattadrūpadhāritvāt // abhts_12.6 vīroddeśena tu viśeṣaḥ tad yathā raṇareṇuḥ vīrāmbhaḥ mahāmarut vīrabhasma śmaśānanabhaḥ tadupahitau candrārkau ātmā nirvikalpakaḥ // abhts_12.7 punar api bāhyābhyantaratayā dvitvam bahirupāsyamantratādātmyena tanmayīkṛte tatra tatra nimajjanam ity uktam // abhts_12.8 viśeṣas tu ānandadravyaṃ vīrādhāragataṃ nirīkṣaṇena śivamayīkṛtya tatraiva mantracakrapūjanam tataḥ tenaiva dehaprāṇobhayāśritadevatācakratarpaṇam iti mukhyaṃ snānam // abhts_12.9 ābhyantaraṃ yathā tattaddharādirūpadhāraṇayā tatra tatra pārthivādau cakre tanmayībhāvaḥ // abhts_12.10

## tsa12-p01
"Initiation and the rest is to be taught" — so it was stated. Hence, for expounding initiation-nature, first to be done, bath is taught. (12.1) And bath is called purity; and purity is supreme-Lord-nature-immersion. (12.2) For turbidity-removal is purity; and turbidity is, though in that-one-formed, conceit of other-form-mixture not-that-natured. (12.3) That here, in autonomous-bliss-consciousness-only-pith, in own self or in universe too, conceit of other-form-mixture is impurity; and it is removed by great-Bhairava-immersion. And it too, for someone, may be sudden; for another, watching with other-means-face. (12.4) Therein too, by one-two-three-and-rest-division, wholly-partly, somewhere, for someone, sometime, thus, from assurance-obtaining, varied is division. (12.5) And it is eightfold: in eight forms earth-water-wind-fire-ether-moon-sun-self-formed — visualized as Lord-natured through mantra-placing-greatness — and through identity, when body is Lord-immersed, from body-and-rest-division-functioning, of consciousness too is Lord-immersion-attainment. But for someone, from bath-cloth-and-rest-pleased-people-producing-ness, it reaches Lord-means-hood — so stated. And stated in glorious Ānanda and the rest: steadiness, filling, vigor, stain-burning, pervasion, creation-capability, maintenance-capability, and nondifference — thus these in them are chief fruits — since of placed mantra in them is that-form-bearing-ness. (12.6) But for heroes is special. Namely: battle-dust, hero-water, great-wind, hero-ash, charnel-sky; in the two placed therein, moon-sun; self thought-free. (12.7) Again is twofoldness through outer-inner-ness: in outer-worshipped-mantra-identity, made-of-it — therein therein is plunging — so stated. (12.8) But the special: bliss-substance gone to hero-base, by gazing having made Śiva-made — therein itself is mantra-wheel-worship; then through it itself is of body-breath-both-based god-wheel satiating — thus is chief bath. (12.9) Inner, as: through earth-and-rest-form-holding — therein therein in earth-and-rest wheel is made-of-it-ness. (12.10)
l2_text:
## tsa12-p01 — bathing
Initiation is next, so first: the bath. Bath means purity, and purity means sinking into the Lord's own nature. What washes off is murk — and murk is taking yourself, one-formed autonomous bliss-awareness, or the universe, to be mixed with some alien shape. Great Bhairava-immersion rinses it. For some it hits all at once; others keep an eye on the means. And it varies — by ones and twos and threes, whole or part, where, for whom, when — as assurance comes. Eight baths: earth, water, wind, fire, ether, moon, sun, self — each envisaged, by mantra set into it, as the Lord himself; and once the body is Lord-dipped, awareness follows though it still runs the body's errands. For some, even pleasing bathers with clothes does it — bath as the Lord's own means. The books of Bliss list what each mainly gives: steadiness, fullness, fire, stain burnt, pervasion, making power, keeping power, no-difference — the mantra set in each carrying its shape. Heroes bathe apart: dust of battle, heroes' water, great wind, heroes' ash, charnel sky — moon and sun set in the pair, self thought-free. Outer and inner make two: plunge wherever outer worship has made you one with its mantra, as said. Finest: gaze on bliss-stuff seated in the hero-base till it's Śiva, worship the mantra-wheel right there, then with it feed the gods enthroned in body and breath both — that is the bath of baths. The inward bath: hold earth's shape and the rest, and in each earth-wheel grow into it.

The passage moves in five steps. (1) Definition: bath = purity = Lord-nature immersion; turbidity = alien-form mixture conceit in one-formed; removed by Bhairava-immersion (sudden/means-facing). (2) Variation: by number/whole-part/place/person/time from assurance. (3) Eightfold: earth/water/wind/fire/ether/moon/sun/self visualized Lord-natured by mantra-placing; body Lord-immersed → consciousness follows. (4) Chief fruits per form (steadiness/filling/vigor/stain-burning/pervasion/creation/maintenance/nondifference); hero-special (five hero-forms + moon-sun + thought-free self); outer/inner twofold. (5) Chief bath (hero-based bliss-substance gazed into Śiva-made → mantra-wheel worship → body-breath god-wheel satiating) + inward bath (earth-form-holding → made-of-it-ness).
